lines.en: it the creator rested from [f. 131] his own works, and

lines.en: that it is a day of idleness and inactivity. For Cronus is idle and barren because of

lines.text: ἄτεγκτος.

lines.text: Ταῦτά σοι, τέκνον, ὡς ἐν συντόμῳ προήγαγον περὶ τῆς κοσμοποιη-
lines.en: These things to you, child, as in brief I have brought forth concerning the world-making

lines.text: τικῆς ἑπταημέρου καὶ πῶς ἂν ἑκάστη ἡμέρα φυσικῶς ἀποκεκλήρωται
lines.en: seven-day period and how each day has naturally been allotted

summary.headline: The Seven Stars and the Magi
summary.text: Discussion of the seven-day creation period and the assignment of each day to one of the seven stars, especially Cronus’s barren and inactive seventh day. The text invokes Solomon and Isaiah, explains planetary configurations and lunar generation, corruption, and renewal, and begins an inquiry into how the Magi recognized Christ’s birth in Judaea.
